elements.text: Back in libbitcoin v2 we used to maintain unconfirmed txs in a "memory pool". That led to problems during the "spam attacks" when we started seeing upwards of 20,000 txs in the pool. As a result v3 eliminated the memory pool, storing validated but unconfirmed txs on disk. Eventually most txs get mined, and we have already validated and stored them, so there is no extra cost - it's actually a great performance improvement. Now with well over 200,000 txs in the tx pool we are humming along with zero performance degradation. I noticed that
blockchain.info
has had a little trouble today with their mempool but cancoin's voyager
has been solid. Nice work!

elements.text:
I've patched a trivial issue in libbitcoin-network that required backport to v3.
Without the fix testnet does stall and mainnet could at any future point.
The problem was an incoorect max size on network messages that can affect segwit blocks and txs.
I've also patched a client issue and similar issue in explorer, whereas witness data is not decoded.
I cheated a bit and retagged v3.4.0 in several repositories.
Also, note that v3.4 requires a resync of the chain so that witness data will be captured for earlier blocks.
Finally, ensure that network.services=9 is set so that witness data will be retrieved from (and provided to) peers.
Also ensure that segwit forks are set (as desired):
Although if not specified all forks except for
easy_blocks
are enabled by default.

text:
I've patched a trivial issue in libbitcoin-network that required backport to v3.
Without the fix testnet does stall and mainnet could at any future point.
The problem was an incoorect max size on network messages that can affect segwit blocks and txs.
I've also patched a client issue and similar issue in explorer, whereas witness data is not decoded.
I cheated a bit and retagged v3.4.0 in several repositories.
Also, note that v3.4 requires a resync of the chain so that witness data will be captured for earlier blocks.
Finally, ensure that network.services=9 is set so that witness data will be retrieved from (and provided to) peers.
Also ensure that segwit forks are set (as desired): <https://github.com/libbitcoin/libbitcoin-server/wiki/Fork-Settings>
Although if not specified all forks except for `easy_blocks` are enabled by default.
